parsed.explanation: The combined national-state regime creates several traveller-facing exposures: sex-as-birth passport/visa rules, refusal of X markers, case-note tagging, possible refusal and permanent fraud inadmissibility; federal facility exclusion and state bathroom bans in public schools/colleges; documented abusive immigration custody; a state felony for gender-affirming care to minors; no statewide nondiscrimination or gender-identity hate-crime coverage. Mitigating factors are limited: no blanket criminalisation of trans presentation, no documented local police sweeps of trans visitors, private services not shown universally hostile, and some national orders are enjoined or in litigation. The state violence figure is an undercount floor and is unusable. The result is high risk, below the Reduced Risk band and near the 0.35 facility-exclusion anchors, but not severe-risk because organised targeting or near-certain imprisonment is not documented.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require sex assigned at birth on passports/visas, stop processing X markers, tag cases, and allow refusal or additional evidence where sex is doubted; suspected misrepresentation can support permanent fraud inadmissibility. Advisories and detentions of trans travellers are reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; fraud findings are not automatic and require four elements; passport policy is in litigation; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign passport and visa checks are unavoidable; an outed or outable traveller faces officer discretion, possible refusal, stranding, or detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports trans men subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; national corrections policies impose conversion-therapy-like measures and care denial; trans prisoner counts stopped being reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some national executive orders are enjoined, but no effective custody remedy for these documented practices is shown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border document discrepancy can move a traveller into immigration detention, where the documented custody harm becomes operative.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars trans use of government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; state has 2022/2024 facility bans, public-school bathroom rule, SB79 binary declaration, and a reported college extension whose status is unresolved.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private hotels are not shown banned; two municipalities have local protections; no statewide public-accommodations right exists.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal buildings and state schools/colleges are birth-sex governed; an adult visitor using government facilities or a minor in school settings is exposed, while private venues may remain usable.

care_services.exposure: State law makes providing puberty blockers, hormones or surgery to anyone under 19 a felony; national policy is hostile to minor gender-affirming care; no insurance protections or statewide nondiscrimination.
care_services.protection: Several national orders are enjoined; adult emergency care is not documented as categorically banned; legal-aid guidance exists.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor cannot reliably obtain care or refills; providers face felony exposure, while adult care access is not explicitly barred but is chilled.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups; justice guidance uses 'radical gender ideology'; state law declares an immutable binary; statewide public support is among the lowest.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Guidance states counterterrorism is not for mere disagreement; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises suspicion and outing severity, though no state police sweeps of trans visitors are documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor faces the state care felony, school bathroom and sports restrictions, national executive-order pressure on teachers facilitating social transition, and no statewide bullying protection.
minors_guardians.protection: Some national orders are enjoined; the adult guardian is not documented as criminalised merely for travelling with a trans minor; private settings may be more tolerant.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent seeking medication or care for a trans minor is blocked by felony exposure; school-like facilities and border document checks compound outing risk.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific incident of violence against a trans visitor is documented; the state hate-crime law excludes gender identity, no statewide nondiscrimination exists, and public support is low. The reported 3.8/100k figure is an undercount floor and is unusable.
street_violence_police_response.protection: The national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; two municipalities have local ordinances; national civil-liberties litigation is active.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local recourse after assault is weak, while national hate-crime coverage exists but local enforcement is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport restrictions took effect; state surgery requirement for ID change was upheld; no statewide accommodation recourse; no effective remedy is shown for facility exclusion or custody abuse.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Some national orders are enjoined; litigation continues; legal-aid FAQ provides guidance.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Partial court relief may depend on which measures are in force, but border, facility and custody exposures lack demonstrated working remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Veluna imposes birth-sex toilets in every public building, rejects complaints and gives no foreign-passport exemption, but has no travel-document regime or custodial care ban. This jurisdiction's facility ban is narrower, yet it adds national passport/visa refusal risk, custody abuse and a minor-care felony, so it sits at or slightly below this anchor.

Teravi has no facility ban, uses working mediators and obtained a police conviction. Here official facility and document restrictions operate with no working statewide remedy, plus severe custody and minor-care exposures, placing it materially lower.

Ilvora has a dead-letter offence, accepted foreign documents, facilities by identity and enforceable court compensation. This jurisdiction has active document, facility and care restrictions and no comparable acceptance or remedy, so it is far below.

Savorek has universal birth-sex public facilities and hospital wards plus police stops and extortion; this jurisdiction lacks documented police sweeps but adds national border refusal and severe immigration custody abuse. It is comparable high risk, not severe.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is not a blanket criminalisation of trans identity, and private commercial life is not documented as universally hostile. But official exposure is layered: national passport and visa rules can out, refuse or permanently bar a traveller; federal and state facilities deny identity-congruent access; immigration custody carries documented severe abuse; the state criminalises minor care and excludes gender identity from hate-crime and nondiscrimination law. Courts block some national measures, but no working remedy reaches the border, facilities or custody. The state violence figure cannot be used. This produces high risk below the Reduced Risk band, primarily because the state itself enforces several traveller-facing exclusions and the severity after outing or detention is substantial.
